srm.expected_ratio_source: dataset card (Criteo AI Lab, Hugging Face): 'Treatment Ratio: 0.85' - a documented summary of a pooled, subsampled dataset, not a per-test design spec

visit.summary: The campaign changed the visit rate by +1.034 percentage points (95% CI [+1.006, +1.063]), from 3.820% in control to 4.854% in treated - a relative lift of +27.1% (95% CI [+26.2%, +28.0%]). That is about 10,342 extra visits per 1M treated users (95% CI [10,056, 10,629]); statistically significant (p < 1e-300).

conversion.summary: The campaign changed the conversion rate by +0.115 percentage points (95% CI [+0.108, +0.122]), from 0.194% in control to 0.309% in treated - a relative lift of +59.4% (95% CI [+54.4%, +64.7%]). That is about 1,152 extra conversions per 1M treated users (95% CI [1,085, 1,219]); statistically significant (p = 7.3e-179).

ate.headline_method: Lin estimator with cross-fitted LightGBM outcome score (see D-16, D-18)

adjust.method: Lin (2013): y ~ t + Xc + t:Xc, HC1 robust SE

evaluation.best_model_rule: highest mean validation Qini AUC across seeds (uplift learners only); test not used

assumptions.label: ILLUSTRATIVE cost/value assumptions - not Criteo figures

policy.units: per 1,000,000 users; profit in units of v unless *_usd

breakeven.note: blanket = treat everyone; profitable only while c/v < overall uplift per user
